subject: Clarifying retention of invoices/usage records when customers request erasure
messages:
From: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@greengrove.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Data deletion request and our invoices

Hi Olga,

We've received a data subject erasure request from one of our end users. Before we proceed I need to confirm Redwood's position: if we ask you to delete all personal data associated with that user, will you still be able to provide us with invoice history and usage records for billing and audit purposes? Our controller/legal team is worried about losing the invoice trail required for accounting.

For clarity: the invoice in question (attached) contains line-level usage that references the end user's email address in the description. Can Redwood remove identifiable fields while preserving the accounting ledger? If so, what does that look like operationally and how long would it take?

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Martin
Senior Accountant, Greengrove Inc.
(attachment: Greengrove_Invoice_2026-11.pdf (PDF, 220KB))
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@greengrove.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data deletion request and our invoices

Hi Sophie — thanks for the note and for attaching the invoice. Short answer: yes, we can help preserve your accounting trail while accommodating user erasure requests, but there are compliance and accounting constraints to be aware of. I'm looping in Neha (Finance) and Karthik (Legal) for the precise line we should take.

High level options we can offer:
- Redaction: remove or hash PII (email) from display fields while retaining the usage quantity, pricing, timestamps, and a non-reversible masked identifier for internal reconciliation.
- Ledger preservation: maintain an immutable accounting ledger record (invoice number, totals, timestamps) that is retained for statutory accounting periods and not returned in full user-data exports.
- Narrow export: provide a tailored export for your finance team that contains the elements required for audits but omits PII (we can run a one-off transformation).

Operationally we typically:
1) Identify fields flagged by the DSR.
2) Run a scoped transform that redacts user-identifying strings and writes a reconciliation map (internal only) that ties masked IDs to invoice lines.
3) Retain invoice-level metadata for the statutory retention period (we'll confirm the exact window below).

Neha / Karthik — can you confirm Redwood's standard retention window for invoices/usage ledger and any exceptions for accounting/legal holds? Also advise whether we can provide Greengrove a redacted ledger export that satisfies both GDPR DSR and accounting evidentiary requirements.

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@greengrove.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data deletion request and our invoices

On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 08:20 AM, olga.petrov@redwood.ai wrote:
> Neha / Karthik — can you confirm Redwood's standard retention window for invoices/usage ledger and any exceptions for accounting/legal holds?

Hi all — quick finance/controls input.

Principles:
- Accounting and tax law (US GAAP / IRS guidance) require retention of financial records for a statutory period — we default to 7 years for invoice and ledger evidence.
- GDPR and similar privacy laws allow for requests to erase personal data, but they also allow for necessary retention when processing is required to comply with legal obligations (Art.6(1)(c)). We treat ledger/invoice metadata as a business record that we preserve for those statutory reasons.

What we can offer Greengrove:
1) Preserve invoice/ledger records (invoice number, total, date, line-level quantity/pricing) for 7 years in an immutable accounting store. These records will be accessible to your billing and audit teams.
2) For any user-identifying fields within usage descriptions, we will either:
   a) redact the PII in the customer-facing copy and in exports delivered to you, or
   b) replace identifiers with irreversible hashes in the retained ledger so that individual user identities are not exposed, while preserving reconciliation (we keep the mapping internally under legal hold only if required by subpoena/accounting).
3) Provide a redacted export now (we can deliver a CSV/JSON via the Drive link) that meets your auditor's needs.

Please note: if Greengrove requires full erasure including the ledger lines (i.e., you instruct us to remove invoice-level items), we will need a signed legal acknowledgement that you understand this may conflict with statutory accounting obligations and could impact tax/audit compliance.

Action items:
- Sophie: confirm whether Greengrove's auditors need line-level PII for reconciliation, or whether redacted identifiers are acceptable.
- Olga: we should prepare a redacted CSV and a short statement regarding Redwood's retention policy for Greengrove's records.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
(attachment: Redwood_Retention_Statement_Accounting_7yrs.pdf (PDF, 45KB))
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@greengrove.com>, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data deletion request and our invoices

Hi Sophie — legal here.

We concur with Neha: Redwood will preserve accounting records necessary for statutory compliance. Practically:
- We will not delete invoice-level records that are required for accounting retention periods.
- We will perform redaction/obfuscation of user-identifying strings in usage descriptions on request, and we will provide Greengrove with a redacted export for audits.
- If Greengrove provides a formal DSR instructing deletion of all traces of the user (including invoice line items), we will escalate and require a signed indemnity/acknowledgement due to the risk of noncompliance with tax/accounting law.

I'll prepare a short legal note you can attach to your internal DSR correspondence; Olga, if you want I can also produce a template acknowledgement for customers that insist on full erasure of accounting records.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
